source.caption: Stretching works, it’s that simple. I had a late-stage post-op athlete who could overhead press and bench press without issues, but couldn’t get his shoulder into position to grab the bar for squats without pain. We stretched his pec major and biceps for two minutes each at no more than a 3/10 intensity, and the tension in his chest decreased enough to let him squat pain-free. Saying “stretching doesn’t work” is like saying “strength training doesn’t work.” If someone isn’t getting stronger from lifting weights, I’d ask how they’re training, because we know strength training works when done correctly. The same applies to stretching, there are different methods and approaches, and it’s just as nuanced as strength training. If you’re trying to increase your range of motion, stretch at no more than a 2-3/10 intensity for two to three minutes and let me know how it goes.
